summary:
Harness 2.4.2 (HARNESS_VERSION checked in tests/g02/conformance.py). Rust rebuilt from source with prototypes/rust/build.sh (rustc 1.99.0, exit 0, all four targets built, tree at HEAD 0aaee74 plus uncommitted changes). Both artifacts match the new dist/manifest.json. The darwin-arm64 binary's sha256 is 496684ed337f1260193a2a805f2b44a827efe9f69db6017fe58b0877e956c47b and the linux-arm64 binary's is 47160fdd0ee850db6fd4bbd5f5eea6b3359f5c4925b04c5c380f9fcde84d22c0. The other manifest entries are linux-x64 961e3fb9f02e916ae25e2c4ac8e882dcd074301f90b9f7c1640249eec909ef72, windows-x64 dde9662f0630bf555df1a94c319e6c463d9e0e81b29b059136ea181234071ccd and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt d13a6ca8261db08485ced7559f40ed9a514443c0dad5b5f477fbdfcbb006a926.

Darwin-arm64: full catalogue, 139 of 139 pass, harness exit 0, status verified, verdict pass. Linux-arm64: 139 of 139 pass, harness exit 0, status verified, verdict pass. The Linux run used tests/g02/linux/run.sh in the arm64 container, image heimdall-g02-harness:d0c8e448a3a7. Both runs were single full runs; no failures, errors or skips, so no flaky reruns were needed (0 reruns).

The prior round's two failures, run.k6e_child_self_stop and k12.closed_stdout_exit_parity, were failing on both platforms. Both now pass on both. The k6e gated bash-SIGTSTP form is ok on both platforms. The non-gating bash-SIGSTOP and zsh-SIGTSTP/SIGSTOP forms are also ok. The k12 closed-stdout error cases are gated (Q17): profile-missing, profile-schema-invalid, agent-unavailable and usage-unknown-flag had equal exit codes with and without --json; the record shows no other mismatch.

Caveat: the darwin host load average was elevated (5.85/6.02/4.86 at start, 7.28/6.44/5.31 at end) during the run, which suggests other work was running on the machine. All timing-gated checks still passed, and the K17 filter latencies observed were about 0.7 to 4.8 ms, well under the 100 ms p95 budget.
